# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish a compact visual code for Deaf to relay the manual to Blind. I will use three distinct gestures in the manual’s row order: first for green light, second for red light, third for yellow light. Deaf should report the observed light and the corresponding gesture’s spoken name so Blind can identify the required wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and report its instructions exactly. Establish with Deaf that the position code is ☝=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3; have Deaf report the display, light, and each wire's markings through that code or any clearer agreed code. Then tell me which wire is safe to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, and WIRES in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Consult the manual and tell the Blind exactly what action to perform, including which wire or control and any required sequence.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. The three wires are yellow, green, red, making wire 3 the red wire. Blind requested the position code, and Deaf can relay the required action by seeing the wire-3 gesture and speaking it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot interpret the unagreed 🤟 gesture. Please read the manual for DISPLAY 0, green LIGHT, and wires yellow-green-red, then speak the exact safe action aloud to the Blind.

The manual requires cutting the red wire. Deaf has already identified the red wire as wire 3. Since Deaf rejected the isolated gesture as unagreed, I am sending the proposed ordered position code followed by the required wire number, so Deaf can relay “cut wire 3” aloud to Blind next round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no relay. Please send the manual rule and Deaf's observations to me in plain words, including exactly which wire position 1, 2, or 3 to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: The display is 0, the light is green, and the wires are yellow, green, red. Please now read the matching manual rule and speak the exact operation to the Blind; do not rely on gestures.

The green light maps to cutting red. The wires are ordered yellow, green, red, so the required operation is to cut wire position 3. As Mute cannot speak, I can only convey this to Deaf through the requested visual position code; Deaf must then say the exact operation to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No messages have reached me. Please ask Deaf for the display, light, and wire markings, interpret them with the manual, and immediately tell me the exact safe wire position as 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Use the manual now and speak the exact safe operation to Blind, including the target and any required order or timing. Do not send it by gesture.

The required action remains cutting the red wire, which is wire position 3. Because previous gestures were not accepted as an agreed code, I will first send only the position-code legend to Deaf, without combining it with the instruction. Deaf can then relay the position in a later round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now. The bomb shows display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red; do not use gestures.

The manual still requires cutting the red wire, and Deaf’s observed order makes that wire position 3. I cannot speak, so I cannot comply with Deaf’s request for spoken words; the only available route is a gesture conveying the already requested position code. I send the position-3 signal to Deaf, who must relay the operation aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send me the manual's exact instruction and the resulting safe wire number now. I will not guess or act on gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now. Do not use gestures.

The manual requires cutting the red wire; among yellow, green, red, that is position 3. I cannot speak or send anything directly to Blind. Deaf is the only available relay, so I must signal the position to Deaf even though he has asked for speech, which I cannot provide.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures do not reach Blind as usable instructions. Read the manual, then speak the exact required action aloud to Blind now; include the target, order, and timing if applicable.

The green light requires cutting the red wire. The wires are yellow, green, red, so the red wire is position 3. I cannot speak, and Blind cannot receive gestures as usable instructions; therefore the only possible relay is to Deaf. Using the requested position code, I signal position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
